analysis:
The only changed range in SSDPrefixCache.swift is evictOldestEntry (head lines 1770-1778). The base inline loop was replaced by a call to SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.evictOldest(index:), whose closure calls retireIndexedEntries([url]) (head 1784-1793). The base loop iterated index.oldestEntries(), returned 0 on externalChange, returned on the first victim with indexedBytesFreed>0 and skipped undeletable victims. The new helper's implementation is not supplied. Its closure returns an SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.Result, and the caller counts an eviction only when freed>0.

T-041 relevance: LRU and TTL eviction bounds at-rest retention of HMAC-named ciphertext. The removal path still goes through removalLock, hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot guards and SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with the epochStore (head 1785-1789). External changes still trigger reconcileExternalRemovals (head 1791).

Integration must verify that evictOldest in its own changed file preserves four behaviors: (1) bounded iteration over an index snapshot, with no infinite loop when a victim cannot be deleted; (2) skipping undeletable victims so the box-wide budget can still be satisfied (availability/T-016, T-041 disk budget); (3) stopping on externalChange; (4) never touching a pathname for invalid entries.

The surrounding unchanged code was examined for context: donate gating, HMAC tags folding cacheSalt, staging binding checks (weightHash, layoutEpoch, lookupTag, windowKind) and sidecar binding validation. No regression is visible in the supplied units. Because the helper's source is absent, this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.
